mechanism_narrative: The observed consistent week-on-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last four weeks indicates a sustained recovery in consumer confidence and willingness to engage in out-of-home activities, which will continue to drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to the mean RETAIL_REC of the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in WORKPLACES mobility, specifically if it rises by more than 2 percentage points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks, signals a significant return to office-based work, directly increasing weekday retail and recreation footfall and driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by > 2 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase, despite WORKPLACES rising by more than 2 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent and sustained upward trend in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility signifies a broad return to pre-pandemic commuting patterns and daily routines, creating a synergistic effect that boosts foot traffic to retail and recreation venues over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases or remains flat, despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES showing continued upward trends.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility, indicating people are spending less time at home, represents a fundamental behavioral shift that, under a regime of loosening restrictions, directly translates to increased engagement with out-of-home activities, including retail and recreation, over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase, even if RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to decline in a loosening restrictions regime.

mechanism_narrative: The recent strong rebound in PARKS mobility at t-0w, increasing by more than 4 points from t-1w and reaching above -10%, suggests an immediate surge in outdoor leisure activities, which often correlates with a short-term boost to general out-of-home activity and RETAIL_REC in the very next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility is above -10% at t-0w and increased by > 4 points from t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases in the next week despite PARKS mobility showing a strong rebound at t-0w as specified.

mechanism_narrative: The recent increase in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, reaching its least negative point at t-0w and rising from t-1w, indicates a return to more regular essential outings and a general increase in public comfort, which typically precedes a broader recovery in discretionary spending and retail activity over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM mobility is above -5% at t-0w and increased from t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM mobility showing a clear upward trend and crossing the -5% threshold.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous and sustained increase in WORKPLACES mobility and decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility signifies a strong and coordinated shift away from home-bound activities towards external engagement, creating a powerful combined effect that will drive RETAIL_REC significantly higher over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises and RESIDENTIAL falls for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases or remains flat, despite WORKPLACES rising and RESIDENTIAL falling for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Despite recent declines, the persistently high level of RESIDENTIAL mobility (still significantly above 10% baseline) suggests that underlying policy restrictions or public health advisories continue to encourage staying home, thereby suppressing the full recovery of RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks, preventing a strong positive rebound.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains above 10% for the last four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days shows a significant positive increase (e.g., > 5 points), despite RESIDENTIAL mobility remaining above 10%.
